data.gender_notes: Arijit is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Arijit is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'ari' meaning ruler or conqueror and 'jit' meaning victory. In Hindu mythology, Arijit is the name of a king, a warrior or a deity who conquers sorrows and brings happiness and prosperity. The name Arijit carries the meaning “Conqueror of sorrows” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Arijit usually hope their child will grow to embody conqueror of sorrows and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Arijit holds cultural significance in India where it is believed to represent power, courage, and triumph. In Hindu mythology, Lord Indra, the God of thunder and rain, is often referred to as Arijit as he conquers the clouds and brings rain, ensuring prosperity and agrarian abundance. Furthermore, Arijit is also the name of a legendary king according to the Indian epic Mahabharata. King Arijit, born as the illegitimate son of King Yuvanashva, was a skilled archer, warrior, and beloved ruler.
data.spiritual_significance: At a spiritual level, Arijit signifies conquering and overcoming inner difficulties and strife. Embodying the qualities of courage, wisdom, and resilience, this name carries a profound message to stay victorious in every aspect of life - personal, professional, and emotional. In Hindu philosophy, every individual is believed to possess a divine spark, the Atman, that is infallible and indestructible. Arijit, therefore, can also be seen as a reminder to tap into our inner strength and remain steadfast in our spiritual pursuits. Thus, this name embodies both the power and triumph that comes with material success, as well as the inner victory and growth that comes from spiritual pursuits.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Arijit: Conqueror of Senses. One who has mastered the inner battlefield of desires and attained spiritual victory.

historical_references.reference: Arijit was a legendary king of ancient India, who is believed to have ruled over the Vanga kingdom in the 1st century BCE. He is most famous for his conquest of the powerful kingdom of Kalinga.

Arijit was also the name of a great warrior in Hindu mythology, who is said to have been a descendant of the god Indra. He is most well-known for his role in the epic battle between the gods and demons, the Mahabharata.
